chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim said: Our companions narrated from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) that he said:

"If there is in a man's house a tree from the trees of the Haram (sanctuary) that has not been uprooted, and he wishes to uproot it, he uproots it and expiates by slaughtering a cow, giving its meat in charity to the poor."
And the boundary of the Haram, within which it is not permissible to uproot the trees, is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for uprooting a tree in the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* specifies the *kaffarah* (expiation) for uprooting trees within the sacred precincts (*Haram*), mandating the slaughter of a cow with meat distributed to the poor. It highlights the sanctity of the *Haram*'s flora, distinguishing between trees that are protected from removal and those that may be uprooted with expiation, thereby linking physical preservation of the sanctuary to ritual purity and charity.
